summary: Friday 23 Oct closed the week with US stocks slightly lower (S&P 500 -0.5% on the day and -0.5% on the week; Nasdaq -0.2% and -0.7%) and the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.99%, while chip-equipment names fell hardest: Lam Research -12.8%, KLA -12.2% and Tokyo Electron -11.0% on the week. Brent crude rose to about $117 (Trading Economics quote, possibly intraday) and WTI to $103.27 as Henry Hub gas fell 15.7% on the week to $2.63/MMBtu; gold lost 4.1% and silver 5.8% on the week. In Asia, South Korea's EWY fund is down 18.5% over the month though SK hynix rose 4.4% on Friday; in emerging markets the Mexican peso weakened 2.2% on the week against the dollar. Turkey cut its policy rate 100 bp to 36% and the Philippines raised its rate 50 bp to 5.50% on 22 Oct, and the Fed (28 Oct), ECB (29 Oct) and Bank of Japan (30 Oct) meet next week. This run could not refresh every item: energy and mining equities, uranium, agriculture and several shipping items carry their 22 Oct values (see gaps).

headlines.story: AI-linked stocks slide after Meta, Tesla and Lam Research results
headlines.summary: The Nasdaq fell about 2.6% and the Philadelphia semiconductor index about 6% on Thursday after earnings revived worries about AI spending, with Lam Research citing supply-chain limits on its outlook and Asian chip names falling earlier in the day.

coverage.title: Wall Street Sinks as Nasdaq Falls Over 2% on AI Cost Worries
Asia stocks slide as AI doubts deepen, Korean chips fall
Nikkei Falls 703 Yen in Morning Session, Breaks Below 64,000 on Lam Research Earnings Chill for AI Trade
Lam Research Sinks 9% as Supply Constraints Cap Outlook; Applied Materials Drops 6%, ASML Holding Falls 4%

headlines.framing: The Tokyo and Seoul-focused reports lead with the Lam Research guidance spreading to local chip stocks; the US reports lead with AI spending costs and Meta's cash outflow.

overlap.reason: Lam Research guided December-quarter revenue to $8.6 billion, citing supply constraints.
The Nasdaq Composite fell about 2.6% on Thursday.
Applied Materials fell with the equipment group.

headlines.story: Meta reports Q3 results, raises capex, and is ordered to pay $25 billion in New Mexico
headlines.summary: Meta reported revenue of $64.6 billion, set 2026 capital spending at $135 to $145 billion and booked a roughly $10 billion legal charge, while a New Mexico judge ordered a $25 billion penalty that Meta plans to appeal.

coverage.title: Meta's revenue surges 26% to $64.6 billion, but billions in settlements and skyrocketing AI spending turn screws on profit, free cash flow
Meta faces $25 billion penalty in New Mexico privacy case: Plans to appeal ruling

headlines.framing: Fortune leads with profit, free cash flow and AI spending; Business Today leads with the court penalty and the appeal.

overlap.reason: Company results, capex guidance and the New Mexico penalty.

headlines.story: Brent at five-month high as Houthi attacks hit Saudi Arabia and IRGC claims strikes on ships
headlines.summary: Brent settled at $111.24, its highest close since May 18, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, while Iran's IRGC said it struck four vessels in the Gulf and three more hit mines near the Strait of Hormuz.

coverage.title: Oil hits 5-month high as Houthi attacks stoke supply fears
IRGC says it struck four vessels in Strait of Hormuz traversing 'illegal route', three other vessels hit mines in Strait
IRGC Navy Says 4 Tankers Hit in Persian Gulf

headlines.framing: The Reuters report leads with price and the Houthi advance on Saudi sites; Tasnim relays the IRGC account of ships using an 'illegal' mined route, with no independent confirmation.

overlap.reason: Brent futures reached a five-month high.
Aramco told staff to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters.

headlines.story: Turkey cuts policy rate 100 bp to 36%
headlines.summary: The Central Bank of Turkiye cut its one-week repo rate from 37% to 36%, its first cut since January, citing slowing inflation (29.73% in September) while warning that high energy prices are an upside risk.

coverage.title: Turkiye cuts policy rate by 100 bps in first easing since January
Turkiye Cuts Key Interest Rate to 36%, First Cut in Months
Turkey cuts interest rate to 36 percent in first reduction in 9 months

headlines.framing: Xinhua and Asharq Al-Awsat lead with the cut and falling official inflation; Turkish Minute adds the ENAG estimate of 46.61% against the official 29.73%.

overlap.reason: Lira rates depend on policy rate and inflation.

headlines.story: French 10-year yield tops 5% ahead of Moody's review
headlines.summary: France's 10-year yield rose above 5% for the first time since 2002 on budget doubts, with the spread over Germany at its widest since 2011 or 2012, and Moody's due to review France's rating on Friday 23 October.

coverage.title: The Euro gets the PMIs first and France's credit rating over the weekend

headlines.framing: Outlets date the spread's widest point differently (since 2011 or since 2012) and use different spread figures.

overlap.reason: French yields feed into euro-area funding conditions.

climate.headline: NOAA: El Nino Advisory, strong to very strong event likely
climate.detail: CPC gives above 83% odds of a strong-to-very-strong El Nino through Jan-Mar 2027 and 83% for a record-strength (RONI +2.5C or more) Oct-Dec; Nino-3.4 was +2.1C. Next update 12 November.
climate.source: NOAA Climate Prediction Center ENSO discussion, 2026-10-08

climate.headline: Typhoon Champi closes Taiwan offices, schools and stock market
climate.detail: Winds of 173 km/h with 600-900 mm of rain forecast for northern mountains through Saturday; the Taiwan Stock Exchange was shut Friday and more than 150 flights were cancelled Thursday.
climate.source: Taipei Times citing Central Weather Administration and CNA, 2026-10-23

climate.headline: COP31 opens 9 November in Antalya; Article 6 moves to implementation
climate.detail: UNFCCC lists COP31 at Antalya 9-20 Nov, run by Turkiye with Australia leading negotiations. A tracker says carbon-market rules are moving to authorisations, registries and transfers; no COP31 Article 6 agenda detail was confirmed.
climate.source: UNFCCC Road to Antalya page (accessed 2026-10-23); Planet Brief tracker updated 2026-10-13

climate.headline: East Africa forecast wetter October-December, with flood risk
climate.detail: ICPAC puts odds above 90% of wetter-than-average rain in southern Ethiopia, central-southern Somalia and northeastern Kenya, with El Nino and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole as drivers.

climate.headline: PAGASA: Philippine drought areas to rise from 17 to 84 by March 2027
climate.detail: El Nino has affected 223,214 farmers in 14 regions with about P6.87 billion in damage; 106 cities and municipalities are under a state of calamity.
climate.source: PAGASA outlook as reported by Philippine Daily Inquirer, 2026-10-07
